title: When Certificates Fail: A Story of Bypassed MFA in Remote Access

preconditions: A login flow has a distinct second-factor step that can be skipped, brute-forced, or whose result is trusted from the client

process.action: Map the full login sequence and identify the exact request that marks 2FA as satisfied
process.expected_observation: A specific response/parameter (e.g. mfa_verified=true) indicates second-factor completion

process.action: Attempt to access post-login resources directly after only completing step one (password), skipping the 2FA request entirely
process.expected_observation: Protected resource accessible without ever submitting a valid second factor

process.action: Test the second-factor code for brute-forceability (short numeric OTP, no lockout/rate limit)
process.expected_observation: Correct OTP found via exhaustive/high-volume guessing without being locked out

process.action: Test whether the 2FA verification result is trusted from a client-controllable parameter rather than re-checked server-side
process.expected_observation: Setting a client-side flag/parameter marks the session as MFA-verified without actual verification

impact: Complete bypass of the account's second authentication factor, negating its security benefit
Account takeover even when the victim has MFA enabled
remediation: Enforce second-factor completion as a required server-side session state, checked on every sensitive request
Rate-limit and lock out OTP attempts; use sufficiently long/random codes
Never trust a client-supplied flag as proof that verification occurred
